analysis:
Examined both files' metadata, all supplied patches and source excerpts against the canonical definition index and supplied T-041 detail. These units change documentation, not executable controls. changelog.d/glm-variable-frame-rate-video.md:3–4 describes accepting GLM variable-frame-rate tracks and adding mov/x-m4v labels to shared ingestion while retaining byte-based MP4/QuickTime identification. docs/architecture/inference.md head:810–813 documents presentation-order indexing using nominalFrameRate; head:829 retains deterministic processor refusals, and head:1896–1899 documents the widened label gate. No independently supported security regression is established by these documentation changes.
Relevant integration concerns are adversarial media parsing and availability at TB-007, plaintext custody at A-001/T-050, cancellation at T-010, and media exclusion from prefix reuse under T-041. The patch retains claims of a 512 MiB decoded-frame cap, prepared-token limits, no media prefix lookup/capture and no media speculation. Surrounding BASE text describes separate Nemotron ingress reservations, codec/frame-count/pixel limits and bounded cancellable decoding (inference.md:95–145); the changelog explicitly leaves its label policy separate. Authorization, attestation, encryption, billing and privileged-helper controls have no visible changes in these units.
Implementation remains unverified: the next pass should inspect changed GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset sampling and MediaIngest.admittedVideoDataURIHeaders/container dispatch. Confirm malformed or extreme frame rates and VFR sample counts cannot bypass decode-work, memory, duration or cancellation limits, and that new labels retain memory-backed video custody. Documentation alone cannot establish those contracts; no missing control is inferred.
